rationale: Selected matched-control campaign. E1 is a low-A experiment at 95 C; E2 and E3 compare A0=0.1 versus 1.0 M at the same 75 C, B0=1.5 M and sampling times. This tests M4's A-dependent impurity branch against M2's charge-independent branching ratio. The original low-A, matched-control and lean designs were compared under six assumed noise/parameter-spread scenarios. The matched-control design was more robust in these conditional simulations, at higher material cost. It uses 1.5 g A and 18 samples. All three runs are committed together. Simulated classification is not a real success probability; the design extrapolates to new stoichiometries and assumes M2/M4.
